meanings.note: под мою ответственность = on my responsibility

examples.trans: It's my responsibility.
On my personal responsibility.

examples.text: Хорошо, давайте три. Под мою личную ответственность.
examples.trans: All right, let's say three. On my personal responsibility.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strange, odd').

examples.trans: She's really strange.
What a strange man!
Tolya, she's really strange.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'thing; piece' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('piece, item') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Life is a complicated thing.

examples.text: А жизнь — сложная штука. Вы понимаете, о чём я?
examples.trans: And life is a complicated thing. Do you understand what I am talking about?
And life is a complicated thing.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun
Secondary conversational sense ('alone') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Give me just one.
I have one brother.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: с другой стороны = on the other hand
Secondary conversational sense ('direction') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: On the other hand, it's interesting.
The shop is on that side.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.trans: She's a lecturer.
I haven't heard of her.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be afraid'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.
I'm not afraid.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').
Secondary conversational sense ('different') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Could we go somewhere else?
That's a different building.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
Secondary conversational sense ('namely') (а именно = namely) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Exactly, quite right.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'thanks to' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: And it is all thanks to you.
It is what earns us respect.

examples.text: Но благодаря вам у нас все получилось. Спасибо вам за вас.
examples.trans: But thanks to you, we made it work. Thank you for being you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'воёвывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to win, to conquer', paired with 'завоевать'.

examples.trans: It is what earns us respect.

examples.text: Именно благодаря качеству мы завоёвываем уважение гостей.
examples.trans: It is precisely thanks to quality that we win the respect of guests.

examples.text: Талантливый повар быстро завоёвывает авторитет на кухне.
examples.trans: A talented cook quickly wins authority in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'важение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'respect' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It is what earns us respect.

examples.text: Именно благодаря честному труду мы завоёвываем уважение гостей.
examples.trans: It is precisely through honest work that we earn the respect of guests.

examples.text: На этой кухне каждый повар пользуется заслуженным уважением.
examples.trans: In this kitchen every cook enjoys well-deserved respect.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

становиться.gloss: to become, to get, to grow

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тановиться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to become', forming an aspectual pair with 'стать'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: And you are becoming an alcoholic.
And you are becoming an alcoholic. Goodbye!
It is getting very cold outside.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'close', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: We have grown closer.
This is my close friend.

examples.text: Слушайте, Марина, мы с вами стали ближе!
examples.trans: Listen, Marina, the two of us have grown closer!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.
He's my friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'to' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.
I'm going to Mum's.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овершать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to commit', forming an aspectual pair with 'совершить'.

examples.trans: You are making a huge mistake.
He often carries out courageous deeds.
You are making a huge mistake, Stepanych!

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'без-' ('without, -less') (stem 'ответственный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('irresponsible').

examples.trans: When we act irresponsibly...

examples.text: Это был очень безответственный поступок с твоей стороны.
examples.trans: That was a very irresponsible act on your part.

examples.text: Шеф не терпит безответственных людей на своей кухне.
examples.trans: The chef does not tolerate irresponsible people in his kitchen.

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'act'.

examples.trans: I committed a very foolish act.

examples.text: Это был благородный и смелый поступок.
examples.trans: It was a noble and brave deed.

examples.text: Соколов, не делай сейчас таких глупых поступков.
examples.trans: Sokolov, do not do such foolish deeds right now.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: What are you doing?
I'm making dinner.
Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'correct' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: A course of the correct antibiotics.
That is the correct answer.
We have prescribed a course of the correct antibiotics.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'conclusion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Из этой неприятной истории каждый повар должен сделать правильный вывод.
examples.trans: From this unpleasant story every cook must draw the right conclusion.

examples.text: Шеф быстро пришёл к выводу, что соус нужно готовить заново.
examples.trans: The chef quickly came to the conclusion that the sauce needs to be made anew.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'work', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('job') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm going to work.
There's a lot of work.
I'm at work.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'more'.
Secondary conversational sense ('bigger') (comparative of большой) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.
I don't need any more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to drink', forming an aspectual pair with 'выпить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
used on its own: он пьёт = he drinks

examples.trans: I'm drinking tea.
He doesn't drink.

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become
Secondary conversational sense ('to solve') (решить задачу) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The court has decided.
I've decided.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Secondary conversational sense ('exactly, precisely') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Lyolya will definitely come!

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'it is necessary'.

examples.trans: It needs a wash.
We need to do even more.
It needs a wash!

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'метить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to celebrate, to note', paired with 'отмечать'.

examples.trans: But we should celebrate that.
We need to celebrate this.

examples.text: Я хотел отметить день рождения вместе.
examples.trans: I wanted to celebrate the birthday together.

meanings.note: + dative of the person, + accusative of the drink

examples.trans: Are you pouring me vodka?
Mum is pouring tea.

examples.text: Ты мне сейчас водку наливаешь, да?
examples.trans: Right now you're pouring me vodka, aren't you?
